get.summary:
The current rate to convert one unit of from into
to. 503 is this endpoint's distinctive failure: the provider's own
retry budget (ADR 0014) has already been exhausted by the time one reaches a caller here.

get.summary: Lists the catalogue newest first, one page at a time.

put.summary: Replaces a product's editable fields. The sku is not among them.

post.summary:
Marks one of the caller's own orders as shipped. 409 if it has already shipped or was
cancelled — an illegal transition is a conflict with existing state, not a malformed
request.

Cancels one of the caller's own orders. 409 if it has already shipped or was already
cancelled.

Marks one notification read. Idempotent — marking an already-read one answers 200 with a
MarkedCount of zero, not an error.
Creates an account and signs it in.

Signs out, clearing the session cookie.

CancelOrderRequest.description:
The reason is owned by `CancelOrderValidator`, not duplicated here as a DataAnnotation —
see the note on PlaceOrderRequest.

CreateProductRequest.description:
Business-rule validation (non-empty, max length, price range and scale) is owned by
`CreateProductValidator` in the validation behavior — not duplicated here as
DataAnnotations. See `src/Api/CLAUDE.md`.

rememberMe.description:
Whether the session cookie outlives the browser session. Maps to the auth cookie's
IsPersistent, which is the whole of what "remember me" means under cookie authentication.

NotificationKind.description:
What a notification is about. Persisted by name rather than by number (see the EF
configuration), so the numeric values here are free to be reordered — but the NAMES are a
stored contract: renaming one orphans every row already written under the old name.

markedCount.description:
How many this call actually changed. Zero is a success: re-reading something already read
is idempotent, not an error.

unreadCount.description: The badge count after the change, so the client needs no second round-trip.

NotificationReadResponse.description: What both mark-read endpoints answer with.

kind.description:
Serialized as its NAME, not its number — `Program.cs` configures a
`JsonStringEnumConverter`, and the generated OpenAPI document and
`frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` both carry it as a string union. A client switching on
this gets a compile error when a kind is added, rather than an unhandled integer.

subjectId.description:
The order or product this is about, for deep-linking. Null when the subject is gone or was
never recorded — see `Notification.SubjectId`.

readAt.description: Null while unread. The single source of read-ness; there is no separate flag.

productId.description:
The catalogue product as it was when the order was placed. Null on orders that predate the
catalogue link — those render as the bare sku with no price.

The catalogue product as it was when the order was placed. Null on orders that predate the
catalogue link — those render as the bare sku with no price.

OrderStatus.description:
Where an order is in its life. Persisted by name, like
NotificationKind — the names are a stored contract.

OrderStatus.Placed is first so that it is also the CLR default: rows written before this
column existed materialize as Placed, which is what they were.

OrderStatusResponse.description: What both transition endpoints answer with, so a client can render the new state.

PlaceOrderRequest.description:
Business-rule validation (non-empty, max length, positive quantity) is owned by
`PlaceOrderValidator` in the validation behavior — not duplicated here as
DataAnnotations. See `src/Api/CLAUDE.md`.

RegisterRequest.description:
Business-rule validation (length, charset, password policy) is owned by the validators in
`src/Application/Users`, not duplicated here as DataAnnotations. See `src/Api/CLAUDE.md`.

SessionResponse.description: Who the caller is. Carries no password material, by construction.

UnreadCountResponse.description: The badge count, on its own so a client polling it transfers one number.

UpdateProductRequest.description:
No Sku: it is the catalogue's business key and the domain refuses to change it. No Id
either — that comes from the route, so a body that disagreed with the URL could not arise.
